text: Where X is a partnership, or limited partnership, then a partner of the partnership or limited partnership.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Where X is a company, then a member of the board of directors or an individual for the time being holding the office of chairperson or chief executive officer of the company.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Where X is the limited liability partnership, then it would be a partner or manager of the limited liability partnership and, I think, in other cases it would be persons principally responsible for the management and conduct of X's business activities in providing corporate activities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that is set out in the Act.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then I think he asked what if any of the key appointment holders did not successfully complete the prescribed course of training and what is the level of intensity or duration of such courses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So the course is mandatory at the point of the CSP's registration or renewal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Subsequently, of course, the CSPs must ensure that the employees are adequately trained in the AML/CFT laws and regulations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, Mr Speaker, Sir, let me conclude by thanking the Members for their support of the two Bills.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Since then, however, money laundering has been a prominent topic in the media.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Your efforts are not in vain, they are deeply appreciated and crucial in maintaining Singapore's reputation as a trusted business hub.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think the first, in terms of the nominee directors, my proposal is not so much about the capping of the nominee directorship per se.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: But I think in ACRA's original consultation paper, they did suggest that for those who hold more than a legally prescribed number of nominee directorships, then you will have to satisfy the prescribed training requirements.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I also acknowledge Minister's point about the enhanced supervisory and enforcement effort, so, I think that is definitely necessary and important.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: But my question is more of, why is it that we cannot have the enhanced supervision while prescribing the minimum prescribed training requirements for those who hold excessive number of nominee directorships?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: The second is in terms of the key appointment holders.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Indeed, just a small clarification because given the definition of the key appointment holders for, basically, those who are principally responsible for the management and conduct of X's business activities.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: In that sense, the question is more of when it comes to someone who is holding a – whether it is a junior assistant managerial position, the level of requirement versus that of, say, the qualified individual supervising the CSP, whether or not then there is a distinction there and, I think, some of CSPs may be concerned that every single manager that I have would be covered.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if it is a junior officer in the company who does not really have a lot of responsibility for the decisions which are taken, then obviously that person would not be regarded as a key appointment holder.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It would be a question of fact in each case, but I think it is generally recognisable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is not a question of age, because you may have somebody who maybe young, but let us say, in a company that happens to be the shareholder's son.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All the other directors or appointment holders may be older, but if the director's son says this has to be the case, everybody goes along with that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Depending on the circumstances, he could well be a key appointment holder.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, you can see from the definition, that the definition laid out certain well-recognised key appointment holders, which is the sole proprietor himself, the partner, the director.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But you do not want to be so tight that you actually leave out people who may really be the persons having the control or the say.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is why the last provision needs a little bit of room for a court or any regulatory agency, when looking at the facts, you identify somebody who really acts in all ways as the key appointment holder and it would land on that person.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think that would have been in the background when you are setting a certain number.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But what we have moved to in these two Bills, is a regime where: first, if you are a CSP and if you are a nominee director, you have certain obligations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are some people who are extremely good with the corporate governance, the corporate law and they are practitioners; they can be easily be nominee directors for a large number of companies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because for them, the knowledge is at their fingertips.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if you set a number of 10, a number of 20 and then say, that at company number 21, you must go training, it makes no sense.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would not say to a top corporate lawyer, who happens to be a nominee director that, that is something that they have to do, because they are practising that every day.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But it is quite different from somebody else, who, let us say, it is only a nominee for one company, but has completely no idea about corporate matters and is just put there because he happens to be a friend of somebody, but truly, he knows nothing about accounts, or anything.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, even one nominee directorship for him would be too much.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, when we were looking at this, setting a number did not really advance our attempt to strengthen the regime.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we thought it is much better for people to pay attention, think about how much they themselves can actually cope with; whether they actually have the right skills in competencies, have the CSP to look at that, also have the company to look at that and you make that determination.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But, of course, obviously the agencies will keep on eye on that as well.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: I appreciate that my question may not be immediately relevant to the Bill that is being moved today, but to the extent that it applies to future plans by the Government to expand our regulatory framework under our AML/CFT/PF rules, can I ask the Minister if there are any specific plans underway to include the art market within the scope of our AML/CFT/PF regulatory framework?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But art, given its value – some art are very valuable, some are not so – but it is potentially something that could be used in money laundering and we will obviously look at it if it looks suspicious.
